cells.reason: The anchor (EU 2023/915 Annex I 3.3.1.3, 0.30 mg/kg wet weight, in force) covers only the listed lower-mercury species; per the 2022/617 list that includes carp ('species belonging to the Cyprinidae family'), trout ('Salmo species and Oncorhynchus species, except Salmo trutta') and the Pangasius/Pangasianodon catfishes (basa, striped catfish, Mekong giant catfish), but it does not cover tilapia (Oreochromis spp.), ictalurid or clariid catfish, or brown trout, which fall under the general row eu2023_hg_fish_general_500 (Annex I 3.3.1.1, 'muscle meat of fish except species listed at lower or higher mercury levels', 0.50 mg/kg), and pike (Esox spp.), a freshwater finfish, sits in the 1.0 mg/kg tier. Because the product definition names tilapia and catfish explicitly, (a) fails for part of the scope and a 'gov/firm' label misstates the EU limit for those species; the number 300 is defensible only as a strictest-member harmonisation (gov for carp, Oncorhynchus/Salmo trout and Pangasius; read-across or precautionary for tilapia, other catfish and brown trout), so the remedy is a provenance split or a cell split, not a value change. No live same-basis row is stricter than 300 (Bosnia 3.3.3 equals 300; the Guyana 200 row is quarantined).
